meta.doctrine: Every scenario set is a dated, explicit analytical judgment — never sourced fact. Each set is graded against reality at expiry: HIT (the weighted outcome occurred), MISS (it did not), PARTIAL (materially right, wrong in mechanism), OPEN (not yet expired). Misses are kept forever; the lesson field is the product.

entries.lab: Two-night campaign is the peak; de-escalation follows
entries.lesson: The prior-cycle template (sharp exchange, then step-back) broke. A third strike round followed on 11 Jul and Iran escalated to a formal closure declaration. The April/June pattern-match was doing too much work in the weighting.

entries.lab: Sustained multi-night campaign continues, no clear de-escalation trigger
entries.lesson: Correctly the modal outcome, and correctly weighted above base. The tell was identified in real time: two consecutive nights, three GCC states, record toll — trajectory beats template.

entries.lab: Iran executes a stated option — Bab-el-Mandeb closure or NPT withdrawal
entries.lesson: Iran did execute a maximal option — just not one from its own floated list. Hormuz closure was not in the option set because Iran had not floated it. Standing correction: when Iran floats options, ALSO weight the un-floated option it controls most directly. The float is misdirection as much as signal.

entries.lab: Muscat produces a strikes pause; closure stays declaratory
Closure hardens — enforcement fire on any southern transit, round 4
Israel re-enters — the MOU dies in fact

ledger.note: Prior (12 Jul) set still OPEN — its 72h window runs to ~15 Jul — but its base case (Muscat pause) is already failing: talks collapsed 12-13 Jul and Round 4 followed. Weighting shifted toward the contested-stalemate risk case accordingly.

entries.lab: Contested-strait stalemate — strikes continue, talks limp on, no clean resolution
Off-ramp reopens — a face-saving Hormuz-management deal within days
Rupture — Israel re-enters and/or a mass-casualty event ends the deal
